1Welcomes the patient and offers a sit½x

4 Instructs the mother to do the following;
  • • Sit on a chair with legs slightly apart
  • • Tighten the muscles of the urethra as though stopping the flow of urine, without stopping her breath
  • • Then tighten the muscles of the vagina and anal area
  • • Tells her to hold the contraction for ten seconds, then release

1Quickly introduces self and asks crowds to step back½x
2Quickly assesses the venue to confirm it is safe for casuality examination1
3 Proceeds to perform initial assessment;
  • Forms general impression of patient
    • Body position
    • Appearance (colour, haemorrhage, obvious injuries, anxiety etc)
  • Assesses airway and level of consciousness and neurological status
    • Alertness and response to commands/pain
    • Are pupils equal, pinpoint or dilated
  • Assesses breathing;
    • Looks to see if chest rises and falls
    • Listens to hear if casualty is breathing
    • Touches to feel if casualty is breathing
  • Assesses circulation;
    • Checks for pulse and heart beat
    • Assesses hemorrhage by looking at amount of blood gushing out or absorbed in clothes
  • Assesses for shock, pallor, cold extremities, heart rate etc

1Reassures mother, puts on apron1
2Washes hands and puts on gloves1
3 Delivers the head as follows;
  • • Places the hanging body of the baby astride her left arm
  • • Puts the 1st finger and thumb of the right hand on the shoulders of the baby and the middle fingers on the occiput traction
  • • Applies trachea in downward and outward direction, bringing the head into the birth canal
  • • Continues to apply traction and delivers the baby towards the mother's abdomen
  • • Clears the airway by sucking the nose and the mouth

Examiners' Checklist

Key areas to assessScoreDonePartially doneNot done
1Creates rapport and explains the procedure to the mother.½x
2Screens the bed and puts the patient in a comfortable position.½x
3Supports the arm on a pillow covered with a mackintosh.½x
4 Puts up the infusion;
  • • Selects the correct infusion fluid preferably normal saline/ringers lactate.
  • • Removes the piercing needle of the giving set into the rubber seal.
  • • Removes air from the giving set by allowing little fluid to flow in the receiver then fills the fluid chamber to half way.
  • • Uses the tourniquet to locate the vein, cleans the area and gently tap the vein with a cannula, then release the tourniquet.
  • • Secures the cannula by applying the strapping correctly.
  • • Connects the giving set into the cannula.
  • • Adds oxytocin 10 iv into the infusion fluid and mixes well.
  • • Regulates the rate of flow as prescribed.
